the mat is
the doorway.

For teachers and practitioners who feel the practice calling them further: into community, into care, into action, and into the places where yoga becomes lived.

We Believe

We believe yoga teachers are already close to the ground, offering what they can in studios, schools, neighborhoods, and quiet corners of care. This collective exists to help that work feel less lonely and more supported.

Who we are

A community
for yoga teachers.

A space where yoga teachers come to skill-share, find support, and move with purpose together. When the work feels heavy, we help each other listen for what is asking to be cared for. This is where practice grows roots in community.

All bodies, gender identities, sexual orientations, backgrounds, and lived experiences are welcome here. If you are a yoga teacher looking for community, support, and a place to keep learning alongside others, you belong here.

Community-led

Honoring yoga's roots

Yoga was never just movement. It was a whole way of understanding life - born in South Asia, carried through centuries by teachers and lineages who treated it as sacred. We try to come to it the same way. To receive something that ancient is a privilege, and so we gather with the reverence it has always deserved.

Yoga off the mat

What teachers
are up to.

Yoga teachers are often close to the ground: listening, adapting, caring, and creating small ways for people to feel more connected. This is what teachers are already doing in community.

01

Accessible Yoga

Chair yoga, wheelchair-accessible practices, adaptive teaching, and spaces where more bodies can feel welcomed into practice.

02

Walks for Peace

Community walks for peace that move the body as an act of solidarity, presence, and collective intention.

03

Pay-What-You-Can Classes

Community classes with no financial barriers. Because wellness should never be a luxury only available to those who can afford it.

04

Community Organizing

Teachers using their voice, relationships, and presence to support local causes, show up for community needs, and help people move from concern into action.

05

Your Contribution Goes Here

If yoga is fueling something you care about, there is room for it here. We want to know what you are tending, teaching, creating, or imagining.

Skill sharing collective

Teachers supporting teachers.

We believe yoga teachers already carry so much wisdom, experience, care, and creativity. This collective is a place to share what we know, ask for what we need, and support one another without always needing another training, course, or credential to feel resourced.

Reciprocity is part of the practice: giving, receiving, learning, and sharing in a way that keeps care moving through the community.

Stay connected.

Join the email list on Substack for meetup updates, collective notes, and future skill-sharing invitations. Next meetup details will go there first when they are ready.

Join the Email List

Email updates live on Substack so you can unsubscribe anytime.

Tell us what you would love to share, what support you need, or what you are hoping to bring to life in community.

Skill sharing collective

Skill Sharing Form

This form helps us understand the real skills, study, and lived teaching experience people are willing to share, and the support teachers are looking for. We may follow up by email about collective notes, gatherings, and skill-sharing invitations.

This helps us understand who is in the room without making years of experience the point.

Think teachable skills that can support real people and communities: accessible yoga, chair yoga, trauma-informed teaching, guided meditation, pranayama, sequencing, hands-off assists, class theming, beginners yoga, restorative yoga, yin, prenatal-informed modifications, nervous system education, facilitation, community classes, or creating safer spaces.

What education, mentorship, practice support, or community connection would help your teaching feel more resourced and accessible?

We want to support teachers trying to bring beautiful things to life in community, especially the things that are hard to carry alone. Tell us about anything you are working on or dreaming about. We will keep track of these ideas as we shape future gatherings and support.
